description: Taiku network-realism target spec. `sampling` is what the generator draws from; `metrics` is what scripts/realism.mjs measures the corpus against. Numbers are adapted from X/Twitter research (see `sources`) to a 30-account, no-retweet-text, $0-media corpus. Confidence: high = directly measured on X; medium = measured but older or partial; low = adapted/estimated.

sources.pfeffer2023: Pfeffer et al., 'Just Another Day on Twitter: A Complete 24 Hours of Twitter Data', ICWSM 2023, https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.11429 (375M tweets, 21 Sep 2022: 20.8% original, 50.7% retweets, 24.2% replies, 4.3% quotes; media attachments 76.9% photo / 20.7% video / 2.4% GIF; 0.44% of accounts make 50% of tweets; follower median 99)
sources.pew2019: Pew Research Center, 'Sizing Up Twitter Users', 2019, https://www.pewresearch.org/internet/2019/04/24/sizing-up-twitter-users/ (top 10% of US adult users create 80% of tweets; median user 2 tweets/month)
sources.pew2021: McClain, Pew Research Center, 'The Behaviors and Attitudes of U.S. Adults on Twitter', 2021, https://www.pewresearch.org/internet/2021/11/15/the-behaviors-and-attitudes-of-u-s-adults-on-twitter/ (top 25% of users produce 97% of tweets)
sources.twitter2018len: Twitter data reported by TechCrunch, 30 Oct 2018, https://techcrunch.com/2018/10/30/twitters-doubling-of-character-count-from-140-to-280-had-little-impact-on-length-of-tweets/ (most common length 33 chars; 12% > 140; 5% > 190; 1% hit 280)
sources.kwak2010: Kwak, Lee, Park, Moon, 'What is Twitter, a Social Network or a News Media?', WWW 2010, doi:10.1145/1772690.1772751 (22.1% reciprocal follow pairs; heavy-tailed, non-power-law follower distribution)
sources.nishi2016: Nishi, Takaguchi et al., 'Reply trees in Twitter: data analysis and branching process models', Social Network Analysis and Mining 6, 2016, https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s13278-016-0334-0 (reply trees mostly small and shallow; heavy-tailed size/depth)
sources.goel2016: Goel, Anderson, Hofman, Watts, 'The Structural Virality of Online Diffusion', Management Science 62(1), 2016 (vast majority of cascades are size 1 or broadcast depth 1)
sources.goh2008: Goh & Barabasi, 'Burstiness and memory in complex systems', EPL 81, 2008 (burstiness B=(sigma-mu)/(sigma+mu); human online activity has B>0)
sources.golder2011: Golder & Macy, 'Diurnal and Seasonal Mood Vary with Work, Sleep, and Daylength Across Diverse Cultures', Science 333, 2011 (strong circadian rhythm in tweeting)
sources.kehoe2018: Kehoe & Gee, 'Analysing emojis in context in a corpus of Twitter data', 2018 (about 16% of English tweets contain an emoji)
sources.gligoric2018: Gligorić, Anderson & West, 'How Constraints Affect Content: The Case of Twitter's Switch from 140 to 280 Characters', ICWSM 2018, https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.02318 (users write tersely: abbreviations, contractions; short posts are the norm)
sources.wang2021gif: Wang & Jurgens, 'An Animated Picture Says at Least a Thousand Words: Selecting GIF-based Replies in Multimodal Dialog', Findings of EMNLP 2021, https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.12212 (1.56M text-to-GIF reply turns from Twitter: GIFs and memes are a standard standalone reply)
sources.reply_forms_note: No published study breaks X replies down by form (emoji-only, few words, media-only). The reply_forms weights are estimates triangulated from twitter2018len (mode 33 chars), gligoric2018, wang2021gif and kehoe2018, then shifted toward full replies for teaching. Confidence: low.

activity._note: Share of authored items (retweets/retaiks are counters, not posts). pfeffer2023 non-retweet split: 20.8/49.3 original, 24.2/49.3 reply, 4.3/49.3 quote.

media._note: Weights per role. Video folded into image/gif because there is no $0 video source. Kinds: none, image, gif, meme, chart, video, link_card, poll.
media._reply_note: reply weights apply to text reply forms only; gif/meme/image-only replies come from reply_forms (about 6% of replies). Together about 11% of replies are visual.

length_chars._note: Target length buckets [min, max, weight]. Real X skews shorter (mode 33 chars); Taiku is educational so it is shifted up but keeps a real short tail. Never exceed 280; never truncate.

diurnal_local._note: Relative posting weight per local hour 0-23 in reference_timezone (circadian shape per golder2011 and pfeffer2023 Fig. 1).

reply_delay_minutes._note: Lognormal delay between parent and reply: median about 25 min, 90th percentile about 2.5 h.

engagement._note: Simulated counters. Likes are lognormal (heavy tail), scaled by persona popularity/5; replies get reply_factor. Ratios carry lognormal noise.

gif_sources._note: Where a sampled gif comes from. giphy = GIPHY search at generation time (pop-culture reactions, like real X); local = self-made animated SVG on public-domain art (media/library.json). Falls back to local when GIPHY is unavailable or over budget.

reply_forms._note: Shape of a reply or quote, before persona bias. emoji_only: 1-3 emoji, no words ('💀', '😂😂'). few_words: 1-3 words ('this.', 'based', 'source?'). *_only: media with empty text. short: 4+ words up to 40 chars. full: over 40 chars. Sources: reply_forms_note.

persona_styles._note: Multipliers on the base weights, renormalized. Persona JSON may set reply_style to override persona_style.

retaik._note: Plain retaiks (repost with no comment) by personas, shown as 'X retaiked' rows. X has 50.7% retweets vs 49.3% authored, about 1.03 per authored post (pfeffer2023). Taiku targets 0.6 so the feed of 30 accounts is not mostly duplicates. Stored as { id, authorId, retaikOf, createdAt, text: '' }.

media.original.visual_share.confidence: low (X publishes no per-post media share; pfeffer2023 has ~0.3 attachments per tweet incl. retweets)

media.gif_share_of_visual.confidence: low (2.4% of X attachments are GIFs; reaction GIFs dominate replies, so raised)

media.gif.giphy_share._def: share of gif items sourced from GIPHY (rest are local public-domain reactions)
media.gif.giphy_share.confidence: product choice (user-approved mix), not an X statistic

media.safety_violations._def: media items with unknown kind, missing alt, third-party without credit+license, AI image without ai_generated flag, non-allowlisted or non-https remote src, or rating above max_rating

length.median_chars.confidence: medium (X mode is 33; shifted up for teaching)

threads.zero_reply_root_share.confidence: medium (most X posts get no reply; Taiku wants debate so capped at 70%)

threads.depth1_share_of_conversations._def: share of roots with replies whose max reply depth is 1

threads.deep_share_of_conversations._def: share of roots with replies whose max reply depth is >= 4

authors.posts_gini.confidence: low (X-wide is far more skewed; 30 curated active accounts are moderated)

graph.reply_reciprocity._def: share of directed author->author reply edges that are reciprocated
graph.reply_reciprocity.confidence: low (follow graph is 22%; reply graphs are more reciprocal)

time.diurnal_tvd._def: total-variation distance between local-hour histogram and sampling.diurnal_local

time.round_minute_share._def: share of timestamps with minute % 5 == 0 (uniform = 0.2; LLM-picked times cluster on :00/:05)

time.burstiness_median._def: median per-author B over authors with >= 8 posts

text.hashtag_share.confidence: low (hashtag use has declined; estimates vary 1-20%)

reply_form.reply.emoji_only_share._def: replies whose text is only emoji (no media)

reply_form.reply.few_words_share._def: replies of 1-3 words, at most 25 chars

reply_form.reply.media_only_share._def: replies with gif/meme/image and empty text

reply_form.reply.short_share._def: replies of 4+ words, at most 40 chars

reply_form.reply.full_share.confidence: low (real X is lower; shifted up for teaching)

reply_form.quote.minimal_share._def: quote posts whose comment is emoji-only or 1-3 words

retaik.per_authored._def: plain retaiks (retaikOf, no comment) per authored post
retaik.per_authored.confidence: high for X (1.03); Taiku target is a product choice

media_policy._remote_note: Must match the img-src CSP in public/_headers. Public-domain art is stored locally (public/media/art), so Wikimedia is not hotlinked. GIPHY must be hotlinked from its CDN (GIPHY API terms) with 'Powered by GIPHY' attribution.

giphy._note: Beta keys allow ~100 calls/hour; the generator searches server-side only and caches per query.
